The lipid-lowering peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPAR) ligand bezafibrate may have a potential preventive effect on the development of colon cancer in patients with coronary artery disease. Our data suggest that patients with coronary artery disease who take bezafibrate may experience a reduced risk of developing colon cancer.

This is based on the fact that our studies indicate a possible association between bezafibrate treatment and a lower incidence of colon cancer among patients with coronary artery disease. However, it's essential to note that more research is needed to confirm this relationship and establish bezafibrate as a standalone preventive measure for colon cancer in this population.

More specifically, we found that selective screening of patients aged 70 years or older, those with a history of cerebrovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, or peripheral vascular disease (PVD), may reduce the screening load by 40%, while having trivial impact on surgical management or neurological outcomes.
